newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Meyer says EMU pact would be positive.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Meyer says EMU pact would be positive.

text.p: Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer said European Union efforst to achieve a budget stability at a summit in Dublin represented a positive effort to control risks arising from the drive to a single currency.

Meyer said the European single currency project posed a risk to currency stability because doubts would persist even in the best case about whether member countries would continue to meet common and strict budget criteria.
"The stability pact is an expression for the willingness to get this issue under control. That is positive," Meyer told a news conference.

Switzerland cannot join EMU because it is not an EU member, but the Swiss franc is highly sensitive to the ebb and flow of market confidence in EMU because many investors pour into the Swiss franc if they leave the mark or EU currencies.

"We will have years of uncertainty and instability becuase even in the best case scenario there will be a question about whether the countries are willing to keep up with the program even after the start," Meyer said.
